A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cascading KV Cache research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original PG19, LongBench, MMLU-STEM, Wikitext replay, latency, and ablation results, including additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark, Booksum, passkey retrieval, latency, and ablation results. Appendix results include expanded MMLU evaluation and head-policy experiments.

M1.justification: v2 introduces chunked linear prefill, processing multiple queries jointly before updating the cache (Section 3.1, Algorithm 1); v1 describes tokenwise processing. Appendix B also introduces GQA-aware head reduction and permits independent head selection, replacing v1's prescribed homogeneous policy. Cascading eviction, attention-score EMA, and circular buffers already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds Booksum narrative summarization and randomized passkey retrieval through 1M tokens. MMLU is retained in Appendix Table 4 and expands from STEM to humanities, social science, and other subjects. The Wikitext replay scenario in v1's introduction is removed. PG19 and the same six LongBench tasks remain.

E2.justification: PG19 removes both HyperAttention variants and adds BigBird. LongBench adds BigBird and truncated full attention to the retained Streaming LLM comparator, called Sink Cache in v1. MMLU adds full-context and truncated attention comparisons. New Booksum and latency comparisons introduce H2O and SnapKV.

E3.justification: v2 reports Llama3.1/Qwen2 backbones up to 70B/72B, changes sink tokens from 4 to 64, and replaces the cache-dependent EMA coefficient with 0.9999. PG19 changes from 25 books with 2K/4K caches to length-filtered subsets with 16K/32K/65K caches. LongBench replaces fixed 1024/2048 windows with prompt-dependent quarter-length budgets. Strided prefill, digit-level retrieval evaluation, and revised latency measurements introduce further protocol changes.

E4.justification: v2 adds stride-size studies of latency and perplexity and replaces the PG19 cascade-count study with passkey sparsity and expected-versus-observed accuracy analyses. Head-policy and reduction experiments are redesigned for the newer models and GQA. Token-selection ablation remains under changed settings, while v1's EMA-coefficient and cascade-acceptance-frequency sensitivity studies are removed.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports 20 randomized passkey trials per insertion-range/sequence-length cell, totaling 600 retrievals, and explicitly justifies omitting error bars through determinism (Section 7). Figure 6 also introduces polynomial estimation of latency beyond memory limits. These additions do not establish increased repetitions or improved uncertainty reporting for the retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: PG19, LongBench, MMLU, latency, and ablation results are extensively replaced under revised settings. For example, v1's Llama2-7B PG19 comparison at a 2048 window is 7.05 versus 6.97 perplexity; v2's reported Llama3.1-8B comparison at 32768 is 7.65 versus 7.60. New Booksum and retrieval results include average digit accuracy of 42.0% versus 17.8% at 1M tokens with a 65K cache (Figure 8). These are not same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The attention equations and exponential cache-span expression in Equation 4 remain mathematically equivalent, despite renaming approximate context length to token span. v2 removes v1 Appendix B's derivation of the cache-dependent EMA coefficient and adds the explicit sparsity definition 1 - |C|/token-span. These are limited formal changes.

C1.justification: The training-free cascading-cache contribution remains, but v2 makes efficient linear prefill a central contribution, claiming a 6.8-fold advantage over Flash Attention at 1M tokens. Headline evidence shifts from v1's 59% cache-operation speedup and small-window benchmarks to much larger cache-speed claims, Booksum, and million-token retrieval. The claimed LongBench gain changes from 5.6% to 12.13%, while MMLU leaves the headline contributions.

C2.justification: v1 argues that homogeneous head decisions avoid positional misalignment and reports failure of naive independent selection; v2 Appendix B instead favors independent heads in its new experiments. v2 adds explanations linking stride size to dense attention and examines when token span stops predicting retrieval accuracy. Limitations shift toward bounded extrapolation and possible logarithmic retrieval, while v1's general positional-embedding limitation paragraph is dropped.

D1.justification: v2 documents stride settings, revised hardware allocations and model paths, and states that code accompanies the paper as a supplementary ZIP; the archive itself cannot be verified from these PDFs. It drops v1's explicit 16-bit precision statement and detailed MMLU prompting/cache protocol. Reproduction remains limited by missing Booksum-specific settings and Table 5's conflicting Llama3.1 labels and Meta-Llama-3 paths.

R1.justification: v2 substantially reframes novelty around linear prefill relative to SnapKV and H2O, rather than primarily extending Streaming LLM's retained context. It adds discussion and citations for these methods, SEA, and GQA, while removing references including HyperAttention, LongLoRA, and positional-extrapolation work. This changes substantive research positioning beyond the switch in citation style.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, limitations, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. The method gains a separate linear-prefill subsection and reorganizes the context-span and implementation explanations. Latency becomes the first experimental subsection, MMLU moves to the appendix, appendices are reorganized, and a reproducibility statement is added. The title and author presentation also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a prefill illustration and retrieval heatmaps, replaces the latency table with three plots, and redesigns head and cascade ablations as heatmaps and curves. LongBench radar charts expand from two to four comparators. MMLU subject bar charts give way to an appendix category table. Existing attention diagrams receive revised annotations, alongside extensive table and page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the practical contribution: strided prefill addresses a prompt-processing gap in v1 and is tested for both latency and perplexity, while quality comparisons also give Streaming LLM the prefill adaptation. Million-token retrieval directly tests long-range retention beyond v1's small-window evidence. These gains outweigh the removed sensitivity analyses, although the 6.8-fold headline relies on extrapolated baseline latency, and incomplete experimental settings and conflicting model paths limit reproducibility.
